column1: # §5  a real parser-combinator library (audit §1.5). All four rows draw the

def pitem s:String => [ if (eq 0 (size s)) [ {ok:false rest:s val:None} ] [ {ok:true val:(slice 0 1 s) rest:(slice 1 (size s) s)} ] ] end def psat fn p:Function Function [ ( fn s:String Map [ def r (pitem s) if (r.ok) [ if (p (r.val)) [ r ] [ {ok:false rest:s val:None} ] ] [ r ] ] ) ] end def manyloop fn [[a:Function s:String acc:List][Map][ def r (a s) if (r.ok) [ (manyloop a/v (r.rest) (push (r.val) acc)) ] [ {ok:true val:acc rest:s} ] ]] end def pmany fn a:Function Function [ ( fn s:String Map [ def z [] (manyloop a/v s z) ] ) ] end def isdigit c:String => [ and (gte "0" c) (lte "9" c) ] end def digit (psat isdigit/v) end def digits (pmany digit/v) end (digits '123ab')

#     interpreter simply UNDER-APPLIES, and the faithful lowering hands
#     the op only the callee's own arity and leaves the deeper values on
#     the tape. RecordDynApply now reports how many window values it
#     consumed so the collapse site removes exactly that suffix.

column1: # §12 the LIST Function form (NUR086's fix, 2026-08-24). All four words
#     take a Function callback over a list, handing it the ELEMENT.
#     The rows RUN on both lanes; they live here because the compile
#     lane reaches them through an island (fold/scan) or the Stage 3
#     function-valued-operand gate (for-each), which the production
#     corpus's compute-gap ceiling of 0 does not admit.
#     EACH GRADUATED 2026-08-27 (Stage 3) into lang/spec/higher-order.tsv
#     §6, with five shapes it never had here (multi-element, empty,
#     heterogeneous, capturing, and the Function-value form). It islanded
#     for a duller reason than "a modelled fn-value callback frame":
#     lambdaCallbackInputs had a MAP case for each and no LIST case, so it
#     fell through to its catch-all decline before any frame question was
#     asked. The convention was then measured off the interpreter — one
#     input, the bare element — rather than inferred from the map twin.
#     WHAT IS LEFT IS NOT THE SAME SHAPE, and the reason is ARITY. A
#     compiled closure binds its inputs POSITIONALLY (invokeClosureOn fills
#     the unit's leading param slots in order); the interpreter presents
#     them in the CALLBACK CONVENTION for the container, and the two
#     conventions differ:
#       MAP  fold/scan   sig[0] = ACCUMULATOR, sig[1] = entry
#       LIST fold/scan   sig[0] = ELEMENT,     sig[1] = accumulator
#     Measured with AMBIGUOUS param types, so it is a real ordering
#     convention rather than a by-type assignment that looks like one:
#     `fold ([x:Any y:Any] => [x]) {a:1} 0` answers the seed, while
#     `fold ([x:Any y:Any] => [x]) [7] 0` answers the element. The MAP form
#     already agrees on both lanes because the handler's input order
#     matches its convention; at ONE input no convention can disagree,
#     which is why each graduated. The LIST form at TWO does:
#       fold ([e:Integer a:Integer] => [a mul 10 add e]) [1 2 3] 0
#         interpreted 123   (a accumulates: 0 -> 1 -> 12 -> 123)
#         positional   60   (the pair arrives swapped)
#     Supplying the carriers in the other order changes NOTHING — carriers
#     only TYPE the body; the unit's param slots come from the LAMBDA's own
#     declared order and what lands in each is the handler's push order. So
#     admitting fold/scan means making the two orders agree at the seam
#     that decides it: the handler's input order for that form, or a
#     per-word permutation at the closure bind. Fence: lang/go's
#     TestListFoldCallbackOrderFence.
#     ON THE ROW COMMENTS BELOW: for the LIST form the callback's sig is
#     (ELEMENT, ACCUMULATOR). Establishing that needs SAME-TYPED or `Any`
#     params — a probe with distinct types cannot see position, because
#     MatchFnSig reassigns by type, and reading one as positional evidence
#     is what produced the swapped admission above.
#     GRADUATED 2026-08-28 — the five list fold/scan rows that were here now
#     live in lang/spec/hof.tsv §12. The gap was never carriers and never a
